p.text: What is the only evidence that the road was repaired?
options: A note in the district minutes

fb.correct: 'A contractor's bill. Nobody has ever inspected the road.'
fb.incorrect_default: 'A contractor's bill. Nobody has ever inspected the road.'

1.say: A parent asked me what this rule means and I could not tell her. Read it out. 'Applicants must be resident in the district.' That is a requirement. They have to live here. Or it is a deduction. 'They must be resident, because only residents got the form.' Nobody would read it that way. She did. And she is the reader the rule is written for. Then I add an adverb. 'Applicants must at all times be resident in the district.' Now it can only be a requirement. One word, and the ambiguity is gone. The next line says the road was purportedly repaired in 2015. Purportedly on whose account? A contractor's bill. Nobody has ever inspected the road. Then say so. 'On the evidence of one invoice, the road was repaired in 2015; no inspection has confirmed it.' Twice as long. And half as likely to be quoted back at you in a hearing.

grammar.label: epistemic and deontic modality — the same modal, two readings
grammar.form: must / should / may / can + base verb, disambiguated by context and by adverb
grammar.meaning: separates 'I conclude that' from 'I require that'

explanation.en: 'She must be at the office' can mean 'I deduce she is' (epistemic) or 'she is required to be' (deontic). Written English disambiguates with adverbs — 'she must surely be' is epistemic, 'she must at all times be' is deontic — and with the perfect: only the epistemic reading takes 'must have been'. A regulation that reads both ways is a defective regulation.
explanation.uz: 'She must be at the office' ikki ma'noda: 'men shunday xulosa qilaman' yoki 'u bo'lishi shart'. Ravish va perfekt shakl farqlaydi: faqat epistemik ma'no 'must have been' shaklini oladi.

grammar.positive_example: Applicants must be resident in the district; they must therefore have lived here a year.
grammar.negative_example: Applicants must have been resident in the district as a condition of applying.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida bu ikki ma'no turli qo'shimchalar bilan beriladi (-shi kerak / -sa kerak), shuning uchun ingliz tilidagi bir xillik chalkashtiradi.

grammar.label: evidential marking — how you know what you claim
grammar.form: reportedly; by all accounts; on the evidence of; as far as I can establish; it is understood that
grammar.meaning: tells the reader where a claim came from and how far to trust it

explanation.en: English has no grammatical evidential, so it does the work lexically. 'Reportedly' marks second-hand; 'on the evidence of the log' marks documentary; 'as far as I can establish' marks the limit of the writer's own search. At C1 the failure is not using the wrong marker but using none, so that a rumour and a finding look identical on the page.
explanation.uz: Ingliz tilida alohida evidensial qo'shimcha yo'q; bu ish leksik yo'l bilan bajariladi. Xato — noto'g'ri belgi tanlash emas, balki umuman belgilamaslik.

grammar.positive_example: The road was, by all accounts, finished in a single summer; no document confirms it.
grammar.negative_example: The road was finished in a single summer.

l1_notes.uz: O'zbek tilida -ekan/-emish qo'shimchalari eshitilgan ma'lumotni belgilaydi; ingliz tilida bunga alohida so'z kerak.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: A parent asked me what this rule means and I could not tell her.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: 'Applicants must be resident in the district.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: That is a requirement. They have to live here.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Or it is a deduction. 'They must be resident, because only residents got the form.'

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Nobody would read it that way.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: She did. And she is the reader the rule is written for.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: Then I add an adverb. 'Applicants must at all times be resident in the district.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Now it can only be a requirement. One word, and the ambiguity is gone.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: The next line says the road was purportedly repaired in 2015.

body.speaker: Aziz
body.text: A contractor's bill. Nobody has ever inspected the road.

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: Then say so. 'On the evidence of one invoice, the road was repaired in 2015; no inspection has confirmed it.'

body.speaker: Kamola
body.text: And half as likely to be quoted back at you in a hearing.
